one_sentence_story: By examining brain regions that strangely dipped during external tasks in 2001, Marcus Raichle discovered the Default Mode Network — an always-on midline brain system burning nearly 20% of your body's energy during 'rest' to weave memories, model other people, and simulate your future.
so_what_for_you: Stop filling every single 90-second elevator ride and walk with phone feeds: your Default Mode Network needs quiet, uncrowded pauses to consolidate memories and connect creative dots.
